in_arabic.name: لقماتة
in_arabic.meaning: اللقماتة تعني القطعة من الطعام أو الحلوى
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم لقماتة مشتق من كلمة لقمة، وهي تعني القطعة من الطعام أو الحلوى التي يؤكل دفعة واحدة. وردت الكلمة في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنبياء، الآية 27، حيث قال تعالى: 'وَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَضَافَنَ فِيهِ وَأَطِيعُونِ'. يعتبر اسم لقماتة من الأسماء النادرة والجميلة التي تحمل معاني عميقة وروحانية في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: لقماتا
in_urdu.meaning: لقماتا کا مطلب ہے کھانے کا ایک ٹکڑا
in_urdu.long_meaning: لقماتا نام عربی زبان کی لقمة سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کھانے کا ایک ٹکڑا یا ایک نگلنے کے لائق غذا۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں خاصی اہمیت رکھتا ہے، جہاں کھانے اور روزگار کی برکت کو بہت اہمیت دی جاتی ہے۔ لقماتا نام رکھنے والے افراد کو خوش قسمت اور وافر رزق والا مانا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: लुक़माता
in_hindi.meaning: लुक़माता का अर्थ है खाने का एक टुकड़ा
in_hindi.long_meaning: लुक़माता नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी शब्द لقمة से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है खाने का एक टुकड़ा या एक निगलने के योग्य भोजन। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में विशेष महत्व रखता है, जहां भोजन और आजीविका की आशीर्वाद को बहुत महत्व दिया जाता है। लुक़माता नाम रखने वाले व्यक्तियों को भाग्यशाली और समृद्ध जीवन वाला माना जाता है।

in_pashto.name: لقماته
in_pashto.meaning: د خوړو یوه ټوټه، یا یوه خواږه ټوټه
in_pashto.long_meaning: لقماته نوم د عربي کلمې لقمة څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د خوړو یوه ټوټه یا یوه خواږه ټوټه ده. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون قومونو په دودیزو نومونو کې ځانګړی اهمیت لري، چیرته چې د خوړو او معیشت برکت ډیره مهمه ده. لقماته نوم لرونکي کسان خوشحاله او دولتمند ګڼل کیږي.

in_english.name: Luqmata
in_english.meaning: Luqmata means a piece of food or a bite
in_english.long_meaning: The name Luqmata originates from the Arabic word 'لقمة' (luqmah), which means a piece of food or a bite. This term is mentioned in the Quran, Surah Al-Anbiya, Verse 27. In Islamic tradition, Luqmata symbolizes sustenance, blessings, and the act of sharing food. The name Luqmata signifies good fortune, abundance, and a life filled with spiritual and material prosperity. It is a rare and beautiful name that reflects the values of generosity and gratitude.

data.cultural_impact: The name Luqmata is not commonly used in the Arab world as a given name. However, it can still hold cultural significance in various ways. For instance, in poetry and literature, Luqmata can symbolize unity and cohesion, drawing from its literal meaning of a lump or mass. Similarly, the name can be used to denote a collection or gathering of like-minded individuals, fostering a sense of community and togetherness.
data.spiritual_significance: spiritually, the name Luqmata holds deep significance as it can be seen as a reminder of our connection and unity with God and His creation. The name's metaphorical meaning can be interpreted as the belief that we are all part of one divine lump or mass, created by God and bound together by our shared humanity and faith. This notion of unity and unity with God echoes the Islamic belief in Tawhid or the oneness of God, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual bond with the Divine. Additionally, Luqmata can also serve as a reminder of the spiritual journey of the soul, which begins as a small lump or seed and grows through faith, acts of worship, and spiritual development, ultimately becoming a divine entity in its union with the Creator.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah Wa Al-Nihayah (Vol.5, Pg.137) The name Luqmata carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The origin of Luqmata's name is connected to the incident where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sent an army under the command of Ali Ibn Abi Talib to Khaibar. The army was unable to win the battle and Luqmata, the beautiful sister of the Jewish tribal chief, was taken captive. Muhammad (PBUH) was informed that she was a woman of great virtue and wisdom. When Luqmata saw the Prophet, she was deeply moved by his noble character and accepted Islam. She became known as Luqmata Al-Baniyas, meaning Luqmata the daughter of Banu Asad, in honor of her noble lineage.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf (Vol.2, Pg.311) The name Luqmata carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Luqmata, the sister of the Jewish leader of Khaibar, was taken captive by the Muslim army led by Ali Ibn Abi Talib. She was known for her great beauty and intelligence. Luqmata was initially reluctant to embrace Islam but was eventually convinced by the Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) noble character and deep understanding of religion. She became a respected figure in the Muslim community and was known as Luqmata Al-Baniyas.

It is particularly prominent in Islamic art and culture, where it is used as a reference to intricately designed patterns and motifs resembling tiny pearls. In Islamic fashion, Luqmata is often seen as a name for clothing styles that feature delicate, embellished details, reminiscent of pearls. Lastly, in the realm of Islamic beauty standards, Luqmata signifies the pursuit of beauty through small, subtle enhancements, akin to the addition of pearls to an outfit or a piece of jewelry. Pinterest and Instagram are popular platforms for discovering and showcasing Luqmata-inspired content, while YouTube offers tutorials and tutorial series on how to create Luqmata-inspired looks and designs.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Luqmata is derived from the Arabic word "luqm" which means a 'grain' or 'morsel'. In Islamic tradition, this name is given to remind us of the story of Prophet Luqman, who imparted wise counsel to his son, represented by the small yet significant 'morsels' of wisdom. The name thus signifies the quest for knowledge and the importance of imparting and receiving wisdom.
